state.question: How do the chefs in video A and video B differ in the seasonings they add to the flour when coating the calamari?
state.summary: Evidence supports a visual difference: Video A's chef adds a brown granular seasoning and black specks linked to a pepper mill, while Video B shows flour with dark specks used for coating but no visible seasoning-addition event. Exact seasoning identities remain partially unresolved.
inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer is nonempty free text in the format requested by the question.
v1 is Video A and v2 is Video B; preserve this attribution in the comparative answer.

attempts: Video A shows a brown granular substance being added to the flour and black specks associated with a pepper mill; the exact identity of the brown seasoning remains unresolved.
Video B shows flour containing dark specks and later being used to coat calamari, but the cited evidence does not identify the specks or show a visible seasoning-addition event.

The flour coatings differ visually in the cited evidence: Video A shows an explicit brown granular addition plus black specks, while Video B shows dark specks in the flour without a visible addition event.

events.description: Intro sequence: host in 'Aussie Griller' shirt, then title cards Welcome, Barbeque, Meat, Sides, Aussie Griller over food images.
Chef handles white calamari tubes on a wooden YouTube-branded cutting board, slicing into rings and strips.
events.uncertainty: Knife not clearly visible during slicing.

events.description: A white bowl is presented containing two distinct piles of fine white flour-like powder.
Seasonings are added to the flour: first a brown powder is poured, then a greyish powder, then black pepper is ground from a mill.
events.uncertainty: Specific spice names not visible on labels.

events.description: A hand uses a spoon to mix white powder in a bowl, then presses a ring into it. Small dark specks are visible in the powder.
Breaded rings are placed on a hot black griddle. Tongs are used to flip and move the rings as they cook.
Cooked golden rings are plated next to green salad leaves and red tomatoes on a white plate.
A glass bowl of raw calamari garnished with lemon and parsley is shown next to a metal bowl containing flour.
Dark specks, likely pepper or herbs, are sprinkled onto the surface of the flour in the metal bowl.
A man wearing a grey shirt is shown looking down, presumably at the preparation area.
Hands toss pieces of calamari in the seasoned flour, coating them thoroughly before lifting them out.
The flour-coated calamari pieces are dropped into a pot of hot oil, causing vigorous bubbling.
A slotted spoon is used to stir and lift the frying calamari rings out of the hot oil.
A hand pours a brown granular seasoning from a clear glass container into a white bowl containing flour.
events.uncertainty: Identity of the brown seasoning is not explicit.

events.description: The bowl rests with white flour and the previously added brown seasoning visible.
Hands operate a metal pepper mill, grinding black specks onto the flour and brown seasoning.
events.uncertainty: Grinding action is inferred from tool position and specks.

events.description: The video shows a close-up of a stainless steel mixing bowl containing a mound of white flour. The surface of the flour is visibly sprinkled with dark, coarse particles, likely black pepper or dried herbs.
A stainless steel bowl containing white flour with scattered dark specks sits on a wooden surface. The camera angle shifts slightly between frames, but the contents remain undisturbed.
events.uncertainty: Particle morphology (rounded vs. flake) is ambiguous at this resolution.

turns.summary: Evidence supports a visual difference: Video A's chef adds a brown granular seasoning and black specks linked to a pepper mill, while Video B shows flour with dark specks used for coating but no visible seasoning-addition event. Exact seasoning identities remain partially unresolved.
turns.answer: Video A's chef is shown adding a brown granular seasoning to the flour and grinding black pepper into it, while Video B's flour already contains dark specks when it is used to coat the calamari, but the available evidence does not show a visible seasoning-addition step in Video B. The supported difference is therefore that Video A shows an explicit addition of a brown granular seasoning plus pepper, whereas Video B only shows flour with dark specks and no observed addition event.
